statement: The supplied sources do not contain a derivation of the derivative of the softmax function; the result is stated directly without intermediate derivation steps. Differentiating the softmax function \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = \frac{\exp z_i}{\sum_{k=1}^K \exp z_k} with respect to input score z_j yields the partial derivative \frac{\partial}{\partial z_j} \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i = \sigma_i (\delta_{ij} - \sigma_j) (equivalently expressed in index notation as \frac{\partial}{\partial q_k} \sigma(\mathbf{q}, i) = \sigma(\mathbf{q}, i)(\delta_{ik} - \sigma(\mathbf{q}, k))), where \delta_{ij} is the Kronecker delta equaling 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise.

symbols.meaning: input tuple or score vector to the softmax function
i-th component of the input score vector \mathbf{z}
j-th component of the input score vector \mathbf{z} with respect to which the partial derivative is taken
softmax function output probability distribution vector
i-th component of the softmax output probability distribution, \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i
j-th component of the softmax output probability distribution, \sigma(\mathbf{z})_j
Kronecker delta, equal to 1 if i = j and 0 otherwise
total number of classes or possible outcomes
input tuple of action values or network outputs
LogSumExp function of the input vector \mathbf{z}

properties.property: Symmetry in indices: The derivative is symmetric in indices i and k and can be written as \frac{\partial}{\partial q_k} \sigma(\mathbf{q}, i) = \sigma(\mathbf{q}, k)(\delta_{ik} - \sigma(\mathbf{q}, i)).
properties.why: The expression \sigma(\mathbf{q}, i)(\delta_{ik} - \sigma(\mathbf{q}, k)) is algebraically symmetric with respect to interchanging indices i and k.

properties.property: Scaling parameter multiplication: If the softmax function is scaled with parameter \beta, the derivative expressions must be multiplied by \beta.
properties.why: Scaling the input arguments by \beta scales the derivative proportionally.

properties.property: Relationship to LogSumExp gradient: The softmax function \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i is the gradient of the LogSumExp function, \frac{\partial}{\partial z_i} \text{LSE}(\mathbf{z}) = \frac{\exp z_i}{\sum_{k=1}^K \exp z_k} = \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i.
properties.why: Differentiating \text{LSE}(\mathbf{z}) = \log(\sum_{k=1}^K \exp z_k) with respect to z_i directly evaluates to the softmax probability \sigma(\mathbf{z})_i.

properties.property: Invariance under maximum subtraction: Subtracting the maximum value m = \max_i z_i from the input tuple does not alter the output or the derivative theoretically.
properties.why: Softmax is invariant under translation by a constant vector along the main diagonal.

assumptions.assumption: The input components z_i are real numbers and the number of outcomes K is a finite positive integer.
assumptions.breaks_when: Inputs are undefined, non-real, or the dimension K is non-positive.

assumptions.assumption: The normalization sum \sum_{k=1}^K \exp(z_k) is positive and finite.
assumptions.breaks_when: Extreme input values cause floating-point overflow to infinity or underflow of all terms to zero.

failure_modes.mode: Numerical instability due to large exponentiations
failure_modes.signature: Overflow yielding NaN or infinite values in calculated softmax values and gradients
failure_modes.cause: Evaluating exponentials \exp(z_i) directly when input scores z_i are large without subtracting the maximum value m = \max_i z_i.

failure_modes.mode: Computational complexity bottleneck for large class dimension K
failure_modes.signature: High latency and memory bandwidth saturation during gradient backpropagation
failure_modes.cause: Full normalization factor summation and gradient calculation scaling as O(K) per example when K is extremely large.

canon_notes: canon expects a derivation but no source performs one, so softmax_differentiation is recorded as a definition
